text: OIs can also be tried in patients who are refrac- tory to or intolerant of treatment with other antidepres- sants.1,2,4 When changing a patient from one type of antidepressant to another an appropriate drug-free interval may be need- ed. An MAOI (including a RIMA and selegiline) should not be started until at least one week after stopping a tricy- clic antidepressant, an SSRI, or any related antidepressant; in the case of bupropion, mirtazapine, and the SSRI sertra- line the drug-free interval is extended to 2 weeks, and for fluoxetine, to 5 weeks because of their longer half-lives. For the tricyclics clomipramine and imipramine a drug- free interval of 3 weeks should be allowed. Conversely, 2 weeks should elapse between stopping MAOI (including selegiline) therapy and starting patients on a tricyclic anti- depressant (3 weeks in the case of clomipramine or imi- pramine), an SSRI, or any related antidepressant. No treat- ment-free period is necessary between stopping a reversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase type A (RIMA) and starting an SSRI or another antidepressant. Drugs that have been used in augmentation strategies for resistant depression include lithium,1,2,4,6 thyroid hor- mones (liothyronine),1,4,6,36 and central stimulants4,36 such as methylphenidate. Pindolol has also been studied as an augmentation agent with several SSRIs and other seroton- ergic antidepressants.6,36 Another method is to combine different classes of antidepressants. Although this has been used successfully in the treatment of drug-resistant depres- sion,2,4,6,36 it may result in enhanced adverse reactions or interactions and the BNF considers it hardly ever justified; it should only ever be done under expert supervision. For further details of the interactions between different antide- pressants, see under Interactions of Phenelzine, p.418. If the response to treatment is good, the patient should con- tinue with the same treatment for at least 4 to 6 months,1-4 and perhaps 12 months in the elderly;6 symptoms are like- ly to recur if treatment is stopped too soon.37-39 In general, the dose should not be reduced for this continuation phase.1-4,7 Continuing therapy beyond this phase1,2,4,7,40 is a matter of clinical judgement and should take into account the number of prior episodes, any residual symptoms, and the severity of the episode. Maintenance therapy should be considered for recurrent depressive disor- ders,1,2,4,7,37,39,41 and may be necessary for several years, if not indefinitely, in some cases.
